# Dev-only upload endpoint with validation and storage

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

A Vite dev-only middleware accepts the game's upload, validates the body against the existing
recording reader, stores it under `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl`, and rejects malformed
bodies with a 4xx **without writing anything**.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want the dev server to reliably receive, validate and store uploads from any
browser hitting it, following the established `configCsvPlugin` pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` registers `POST /api/telemetry/upload` only for
  `apply: 'serve'` (mirror `configCsvPlugin`); tests assert it is **not** registered for a
  build/production server and that `plugin.apply === 'serve'`.
- A valid body (≥1 schema-valid JSONL record via `parseRecording`/`parseTelemetryJsonl` from
  `scripts/recording.mjs`) ⇒ 2xx JSON confirmation carrying stored path, record count and run
  count.
- Invalid JSONL, zero valid records, or an unsupported schema version ⇒ 4xx **and no file
  written** (assert the recordings dir is untouched).
- The stored file follows the existing `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` naming
  (mirror `scripts/record-session.mjs`), is collision-safe/timestamped, and `recordings/`
  remains gitignored (no committed fixtures).
- Oversized bodies are rejected (bounded size, e.g. the existing multi-megabyte local sink size)
  with 4xx before parsing/writing.
- The plugin is registered in `vite.config.ts` next to `configCsvPlugin()`.

- Parent AC (verbatim): **Server-side receipt.** The dev server (Vite dev-only middleware, `apply: 'serve'`,
## Minimal implementation

- Add the plugin mirroring `configCsvPlugin.ts` (JSON helpers, `configureServer`/`apply: 'serve'`).
- Reuse `scripts/recording.mjs` `parseRecording` / `parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics for validation
  (no new parser).
- Tests run the middleware behind a real ephemeral HTTP server against a temp dir, following
  `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` (`startServer` harness with `serve`/`build` modes).

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.test.ts`
- `./vite.config.ts`
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` (naming reference)

## Dependencies

- F1 (enforcement scan asserts `apply: 'serve'`; gate module is the source of truth).

## Deliverables

Dev-only upload middleware + validation + storage + tests; plugin registered in `vite.config.ts`.

## Goal

As a developer, I need failing-first scene tests that pin the SettingsScene
control-scheme UI and the `PlayScene` application behaviour before the UI and
scene code changes land, so AC1/AC4/AC5/AC6 are test-driven end to end.

## Scope

Add scene tests only — no production changes in this item:

1. `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts`:
   - a Control Scheme row exists in the Controls section and is reachable through the existing focus order;
   - Left/Right cycles the scheme in the ordered list derived from the `ControlScheme` union, wrapping at both ends, and the row text announces the selected value;
   - Enter and pointer click activate the row and persist the selection to `ai_hell_settings`;
   - under `asteroids` the movement rows read **Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse**; under `fourDirectional` they read **Move Up / Move Down / Move Left / Move Right**;
   - both schemes share one binding set (rebinding under one scheme is visible under the other).
2. `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`:
   - with a saved `fourDirectional` setting, the spawned player ship uses four-directional movement (input maps to direct thrust, no turn keys);
   - with a saved `asteroids` setting, the spawned ship uses the Asteroids scheme;
   - the loaded ship-config object and `src/data/ship-config.csv` are not mutated by the resolution;
   - changing the setting mid-run does not alter the current run's ship (applies on the next spawn/run).

Use the existing `src/test/gameHarness.ts` boot helpers and the fake
localStorage helpers already used by `SettingsScene.test.ts` / `PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New/updated unit and scene tests cover each of AC1–AC7 (settings round-trip/fallback, resolution helper, SettingsScene control and relabelling, `PlayScene` application) — this item owns its share of parent AC8 and the sibling test item owns the rest.
- SettingsScene scene tests assert the Control Scheme control exists, is driven by the union-derived option list, is keyboard and pointer operable with Left/Right and Enter/click, and announces the selected value.
- SettingsScene scene tests assert the Asteroids labels (Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse) and the four-directional labels (Move Up / Move Down / Move Left / Move Right) with a single shared binding set.
- PlayScene scene tests assert the ship uses the saved `fourDirectional` setting for four-directional input and the saved `asteroids` setting for Asteroids input, without mutating `ship-config.csv` or the loaded ship-config object, and that a mid-run change does not alter the current run's ship.
- Tests fail for the expected reason before the SettingsScene and PlayScene implementation items land (red), then pass (green) after them.
- Tests are run through the test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope) — never an ad-hoc runner invocation.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts` — row, cycling, persistence, relabelling, shared bindings.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — scheme application at spawn, config immutability, no mid-run change.

## Constraints

- Test-only change: no production code in this item.
- Boot real Phaser scenes via the shared harness; no bespoke mocks that bypass scene behaviour.
- Use UK English in descriptions and comments.

## Definition of done

- The new scene tests exist and are red for the right reasons.
- `/skill:test` (changed scope) has been run and the red state is recorded in a comment.

## Parent AC coverage

Covers parent AC1 (data-driven setting control), AC4 (applied at next spawn),
AC5 (keyboard and pointer operable), AC6 (labels reflect the scheme) and AC8
(tests) from "Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player".
data.title: Test: control-scheme UI and PlayScene application tests

data.author: agent
data.comment:
TDD evidence (red → green) before commit.

**Red** (implementation stashed, tests kept): 17 failures for the expected reasons — `getControlScheme is not a function`, `activateControlSchemeRow is not a function`, `getControlLabels()` missing `controlScheme`, and `expected 'asteroids' to be 'fourDirectional'` (PlayScene booting without the resolved scheme).

**Green**: 54/54 in `SettingsScene.test.ts` + `PlayScene.controlScheme.test.ts`, then the **full suite through the test skill**: 289 files / 6292 passed, 10 expected failures, 0 failures.

**Full suite caught a real regression** (recorded for the record): `RebindableControls.test.ts` seeds a `fourDirectional` ship config but persisted default settings, so the new per-player setting (asteroids) correctly outranked the config and its 'i'-moves-up assertion failed. Fixed by making that suite's saved record select `fourDirectional` too — the precedence working exactly as designed, and evidence the setting really does override the designer config.

**Design refinement (affects the resolver landed in cycle 1):** `loadSettings()` normalises a missing `controlScheme` to the `asteroids` default, which is indistinguishable from a player explicitly choosing Asteroids — so precedence level 2 (ship config) was unreachable from `PlayScene`. Added `loadStoredControlScheme()` (raw, undefaulted field) and changed `resolvePlayerControlScheme()` to take the raw value, making all three precedence levels genuinely reachable. Unit tests updated accordingly.

**File-scope note:** the PlayScene half of this item lives in a dedicated `src/scenes/PlayScene.controlScheme.test.ts` (the item predicted `PlayScene.test.ts`) — it needs its own settings seeding and keeps the 7k-line suite navigable.

data.author: agent
data.comment: Control Scheme row implemented with this cycle's tests (see Test: control-scheme UI and PlayScene application tests (AH-0MVIAQEI600528E2)): focusable `controlScheme` row first in the Controls section (Left/Right cycles, Enter/click activates, wraps both ways), scheme-aware movement-row labels from a `Record<ControlScheme, ...>` map (Asteroids: Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse) over the single shared binding set, `_persist()` carrying the scheme, and `getControlScheme`/`setControlScheme`/`cycleControlScheme`/`getControlSchemeRowText`/`getBindingRowText` accessors. Capture prompt and conflict warning now name the row as displayed under the selected scheme.

data.author: agent
data.comment: PlayScene now resolves the effective scheme once at ship spawn — `resolvePlayerControlScheme(loadStoredControlScheme(), loadShipConfig())` — and passes `{ ...shipConfig, controlScheme: resolved }` to `new Player(...)`. The loaded ship-config object and `ship-config.csv` are never mutated, no live `setScheme()` swap happens mid-run, and the gyms keep their config/toggle path. Verified by `src/scenes/PlayScene.controlScheme.test.ts` (saved fourDirectional drives translation, saved asteroids drives turning, invalid setting falls back to the config, mid-run change leaves the current ship alone, next run picks up the change).
